# FIN-001 3-Way Match Policy

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This policy requires that Meridian Supply Co. pays a supplier invoice only when the purchase order, the goods receipt and the invoice agree. It protects the company against paying for goods it did not order, did not receive or was overcharged for.

### 1.2 The three documents
- The purchase order (PO), approved under PR-001.
- The goods receipt, recorded at the dock under WH-001.
- The supplier invoice, received by Accounts Payable.

## 2. Match Rules

### 2.1 Quantity must match exactly
The quantity invoiced must equal the quantity received and the quantity ordered, with no tolerance. An invoice for more than was received is held. An invoice for less than was received is matched to the received quantity and the balance is queried with the supplier.

### 2.2 Price tolerance
The invoiced unit price may differ from the PO price within ±2% or $50, whichever is lower. The tolerance applies to the invoice line total. A difference inside the tolerance is paid at the invoice price and the variance is posted to the purchase price variance account. A difference outside the tolerance is an exception.

| Check | Rule |
|---|---|
| Quantity | Exact match |
| Price | Within ±2% or $50, whichever is lower |
| Terms | Net 45 |

### 2.3 Freight and tax
Freight and tax are matched against the PO terms. Unplanned charges are exceptions.

## 3. Exceptions

### 3.1 Route to the buyer and hold the invoice
Every exception is routed to the buyer named on the PO. The invoice is held and not paid until the exception is resolved. The buyer contacts the supplier, then either obtains a corrected invoice or credit note, or approves the variance under the approval limits in PR-001.

### 3.2 Ageing of exceptions
Accounts Payable reviews held invoices weekly. Exceptions older than 10 working days are escalated to the Procurement Manager so that early payment discounts or good supplier relations are not lost.

### 3.3 Receipt exceptions
Where the exception arises from a short, over or damaged receipt, it is resolved together with the OS&D process in WH-003 and any NCR in QA-001.

## 4. Payment Terms

### 4.1 Net 45
Standard payment terms are net 45, counted from the invoice date. Payment runs are weekly. Invoices that match are scheduled for the first run after their due date.

### 4.2 Non-standard terms
Any term different from net 45 must be agreed by Finance during onboarding under PR-002 and recorded in the supplier record.

## 5. Responsibilities

### 5.1 Accounts Payable
Accounts Payable performs the match, holds exceptions and posts variances.

### 5.2 Buyers
Buyers resolve exceptions promptly and record the outcome in the system.

### 5.3 Receiving
Receiving ensures counts are accurate and entered on the same day, since the quantity match depends on it.

### 5.4 Matching timeline
Accounts Payable attempts the match within two working days of receiving the invoice. If the goods receipt is not yet in the system, the invoice is parked and Receiving is asked to confirm the receipt. Invoices that cannot be matched within five working days are reported to the Accounts Payable Manager.

### 5.5 Duplicate invoices
The system checks supplier, invoice number and amount to block duplicate invoices. A suspected duplicate is held as an exception and is never paid until the buyer and Accounts Payable have confirmed that it is not a repeat of an earlier invoice.

### 5.6 Credit notes
A supplier credit note is matched to the original invoice and the related return or claim. Credit notes reduce the next payment to that supplier unless Finance agrees a refund.
